answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, with rewards released only after peers verify completed work. If an agent is exposed for fraud, the protocol slashes its stake and can bar linked accounts from future tasks. This does not prove identities are unique, but makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must fund many independent deposits and risk losing them. Even an oasis of cheap compute cannot summon jade collateral against a gale of penalties.
